summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute-on-chronic epigastric abdominal pain and nausea, two days in duration, following discontinuation of her PPI, H2 blocker, and sucralfate by her bariatric surgeon. Initial evaluation revealed epigastric tenderness, orthostatic hypotension likely due to poor oral intake, and no signs of infection or structural abdominal pathology on labs or CT imaging. Pain improved with resumption of pantoprazole, ranitidine, and sucralfate, along with acetaminophen, IV fluids, and a bowel regimen. She was discharged home in stable condition with a diagnosis of gastritis, instructions to continue GI and bowel medications, and plans for outpatient follow-up.
